subject: general
question: In the displacement reaction between iron metal and copper sulphate solution _________.

options.text: iron displaces sulphate from copper sulphate solution because it is less reactive than sulphate
iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution because it is more reactive than copper
iron displaces sulphate from copper sulphate solution because it is more reactive than sulphate
iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution because it is less reactive than copper

solution:
The correct answer is __**option 2**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In a displacement reaction, a more reactive metal displaces a less reactive metal from its compound. 
 
• Iron (Fe) is more reactive than copper (Cu), so when iron metal is added to a copper sulphate (CuSO₄) solution, iron displaces copper from the solution and forms iron(II) sulphate (FeSO₄), while copper metal is deposited. 
 
• The chemical equation for the reaction is:
 
• Fe(s)+CuSO₄(aq)→FeSO₄(aq)+Cu(s)
 
• This occurs because iron has a greater tendency to lose electrons (oxidize) compared to copper, which allows it to replace copper in the compound.

1d7:T1
